concept.name: Funding interval
concept.definition: The funding interval is the fixed period between funding payments on a perpetual futures contract — the clock that determines how often the funding rate is applied to open positions.
concept.intuition: It is the billing cycle of the perp tether: every interval, the payment between longs and shorts settles and the meter resets.
concept.mechanics: Binance settles funding every 8 hours at 00:00, 08:00 and 16:00 UTC; only positions open at those timestamps pay or receive (with a ~15-second execution deviation), so closing before the timestamp avoids the charge entirely. In extreme volatility venues can shorten the interval (e.g. to 4h or 1h) to tighten the peg; the default interest component (0.03%/day) is split per interval (0.01% per 8h).
concept.failure_modes: Interval changes during stress (announced per venue rules) alter the carry economics of open positions mid-trade; timing games around timestamps (closing seconds before, reopening after) add noise and can distort the rate's anchoring function.
concept.misconceptions: Intervals are venue- and contract-specific, not universal — assuming 8h everywhere misprices carry; and funding accrues only at the timestamps, not continuously: intraday holding between timestamps costs no funding.
concept.example: A trader opening a BTC long at 08:00:05 UTC still pays the 08:00 funding (within the 15-second deviation window), while one who closed at 07:59 pays nothing regardless of how large the rate is.

citations.source: Binance Support - Introduction to Binance Futures Funding Rates
